questions.question: Define primary needs and secondary needs and give two examples of each.
questions.expected_answer: Primary needs: needs that must be satisfied to survive and stay healthy, e.g. food, water, shelter, clothing (health care, safety). Secondary needs: needs that improve the quality of life once primary needs are met, e.g. education, transport, communication, furniture, recreation.

questions.question: Explain how a household's income affects the needs it can satisfy.
questions.expected_answer: A low-income household spends most of its income on primary needs and has little left for secondary needs or wants; a higher-income household meets primary needs easily and can also satisfy secondary needs, wants and save. Rising income lets a household move up from primary to secondary needs.

questions.question: Name the five levels of Maslow's pyramid from the bottom, and say what the model suggests about the order of needs.
questions.expected_answer: Physical (food, water, warmth, rest); safety; belonging and love; esteem; self-actualisation. It suggests people usually satisfy lower, survival needs before higher needs become their focus, although it is a model and people's lives do not always follow it exactly.
